## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Lattices
//
// Bodies for the periodic cellular structures of `lattices.types.plato`: the
// named unit cells, the tiling that turns a cell into welded world-space struts,
// the operators over a tiled lattice, and the triply periodic minimal surfaces.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Unit-cell construction
//  - The standard unit cells
//  - Periodic identification within a cell
//  - Readings on a unit cell
//  - Tiling a cell into world space
//  - Welding: which cell emits a shared strut
//  - Readings on a tiled lattice
//  - Operators over a strut list
//  - Triply periodic minimal surfaces

library Lattices
{
    //==
    // # Unit-cell construction
    //
    // A unit cell is a node list in normalized cell coordinates plus an index
    // pair per strut. The cells below are written as literal data, because a
    // cell IS data: its node coordinates and its connectivity are the
    // definition of the structure and nothing derives them.

    // A strut between two nodes of a cell, by their positions in the node array.
    // The spelling the cell tables below are written in.
    Strut(a: Integer, b: Integer): LatticeStrut
        => LatticeStrut(ItemIndex(a), ItemIndex(b));

    // Both endpoints participate in the digest.
    Hash(self: LatticeStrut): Integer
        => self.A.Hash * 31 + self.B.Hash;

    // The segment as a 0- or 1-element list: kept when `condition` holds. The
    // keep-or-drop building block inside a FlatMap, and the reason no operator
    // below needs a filter (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Partial operations).
    // The point-valued twin is `KeepPoint` in `solids-csg.library.plato`.
    KeepSegment(condition: Boolean, s: Line3D): Array<Line3D>
        => (condition ? 1 : 0).MapRange(i => s);

    // The eight corners of the unit cube, in the order used by every cell table
    // below: indices 0-3 are the loop (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), (0,1) in (x, y) on
    // the z = 0 face, and 4-7 the same loop on z = 1.
    CubeCorners(_: LatticeUnitCell): Array<Point3D>
        => [
            Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), Point3D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
            Point3D(1.0, 1.0, 0.0), Point3D(0.0, 1.0, 0.0),
            Point3D(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), Point3D(1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
            Point3D(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), Point3D(0.0, 1.0, 1.0)
        ];

    // The twelve edges of the unit cube over `CubeCorners`: the two z-face loops
    // and the four uprights joining corner c to corner c + 4.
    CubeEdges(_: LatticeUnitCell): Array<LatticeStrut>
        => [
            Strut(0, 1), Strut(1, 2), Strut(2, 3), Strut(3, 0),
            Strut(4, 5), Strut(5, 6), Strut(6, 7), Strut(7, 4),
            Strut(0, 4), Strut(1, 5), Strut(2, 6), Strut(3, 7)
        ];

    // The six face centers of the unit cube, in the order used by the
    // face-centered tables: z = 0, z = 1, y = 0, y = 1, x = 0, x = 1. They take
    // indices 8-13 when appended to `CubeCorners`.
    CubeFaceCenters(_: LatticeUnitCell): Array<Point3D>
        => [
            Point3D(0.5, 0.5, 0.0), Point3D(0.5, 0.5, 1.0),
            Point3D(0.5, 0.0, 0.5), Point3D(0.5, 1.0, 0.5),
            Point3D(0.0, 0.5, 0.5), Point3D(1.0, 0.5, 0.5)
        ];

    //==
    // # The standard unit cells
    //
    // The cells a lattice tool is expected to name, each dispatched on
    // `LatticeUnitCell` following the tree's constant idiom and read as
    // `LatticeUnitCell.OctetTruss`. Every one satisfies the periodicity
    // precondition in `lattices.types.plato`, so the tiling welds them without
    // a search.
    //
    // The number in each comment is the node's coordination number ONCE TILED —
    // how many struts meet at it in the infinite lattice, which is not the
    // number of struts touching it inside one cell. `NodeValences` recomputes it
    // from any cell.

    // The simple cubic cell: the eight cube corners joined by the twelve cube
    // edges. Coordination 6, and bending-dominated — the softest of the cells
    // here, because nothing triangulates its square faces.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_crystal_system)
    SimpleCubic(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners, LatticeUnitCell.CubeEdges);

    // The body-centered cubic cell: a node at the cell center joined to all
    // eight corners, with no cube edges. Coordination 8 at both the center and
    // the corner. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubic_crystal_system)
    BodyCenteredCubic(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(
            LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners.Append(Point3D(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)),
            [
                Strut(8, 0), Strut(8, 1), Strut(8, 2), Strut(8, 3),
                Strut(8, 4), Strut(8, 5), Strut(8, 6), Strut(8, 7)
            ]);

    // The face-centered cubic cell: each face center joined to the four corners
    // of its own face. Coordination 12 at a corner and 4 at a face center. This
    // is the additive-manufacturing FCC cell, which is the octet truss below
    // with the octahedron left out.
    FaceCenteredCubic(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(
            LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners.Concatenate(LatticeUnitCell.CubeFaceCenters),
            LatticeUnitCell.FaceDiagonalStruts);

    // The twenty-four struts joining each face center (indices 8-13) to the four
    // corners of its own face. Shared by the face-centered cubic and octet cells.
    FaceDiagonalStruts(_: LatticeUnitCell): Array<LatticeStrut>
        => [
            Strut(8, 0), Strut(8, 1), Strut(8, 2), Strut(8, 3),
            Strut(9, 4), Strut(9, 5), Strut(9, 6), Strut(9, 7),
            Strut(10, 0), Strut(10, 1), Strut(10, 5), Strut(10, 4),
            Strut(11, 3), Strut(11, 2), Strut(11, 6), Strut(11, 7),
            Strut(12, 0), Strut(12, 3), Strut(12, 7), Strut(12, 4),
            Strut(13, 1), Strut(13, 2), Strut(13, 6), Strut(13, 5)
        ];

    // The octet truss: the face-centered cell plus the twelve edges of the
    // octahedron its six face centers form. Every strut has the same length and
    // every node has coordination 12; it is fully triangulated and therefore
    // stretch-dominated, which is why it is the default choice for stiffness at
    // low density. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octet_truss)
    OctetTruss(_: LatticeUnitCell): LatticeUnitCell
        => LatticeUnitCell(
            LatticeUnitCell.CubeCorners.Concatenate(LatticeUnitCell.CubeFaceCenters),
            LatticeUnitCell.FaceDiagonalStruts.Concatenate([
                Strut(8, 10), Strut(8, 11), Strut(8, 12), Strut(8, 13),
                Strut(9, 10), Strut(9, 11), Strut(9, 12), Strut(9, 13),
                Strut(10, 12), Strut(10, 13), Strut(11, 12), Strut(11, 13)
            ]));
```
